trigger: an execution is cancelled while its agent is still genuinely running (no gRPC kill RPC exists)
summary: mark_cancelled bulk-released every open concurrency claim on the execution, admitting a duplicate per-device dispatch to a still-executing agent -- the exact race this feature exists to prevent.
classification_rationale: code behavior directly contradicted the feature's own stated purpose

trigger: ScheduleRunner::dispatch_tracked's second get_definition() read (needed for concurrency_mode) fails or returns empty
summary: the concurrency gate was silently disarmed with no log line, no counter, no signal -- a schedule fire dispatched fully ungated with nothing to show for it.
classification_rationale: a fail-open path with zero observability, silent by omission

trigger: a confined operator names an out-of-scope agent id in a Group/Scope/Ids dispatch of a per-device definition
summary: resolve_and_dispatch_confined claimed a concurrency slot against the raw, unfiltered candidate list before authz::filter_to_scope narrowed it -- an out-of-scope agent could consume/hold a concurrency claim slot it was never entitled to dispatch against, an availability side-channel.
classification_rationale: authz filter applied too late in the claim/dispatch sequence

trigger: an operator or agentic caller reads docs/user-manual/instructions.md section 8 for the concurrency model
summary: section 8 still described all 5 concurrency modes as fully implemented including a never-built wait queue, and explicitly RECOMMENDED per-definition for 'dangerous global operations (schema migration, bulk delete)' -- a false safety claim, since that mode was never enforced. Independently flagged by docs-writer, sre, compliance-officer, and enterprise-readiness (4-way convergence).
classification_rationale: documentation asserted a safety guarantee the code never implemented

trigger: reviewing the DirectorySync::sync_entra guard's RAII Release helper
summary: the guard held a raw std::atomic<bool>* rather than a reference, unlike the nvd_sync.cpp ActiveGuard precedent for the same pattern elsewhere in the codebase.
classification_rationale: style/precedent deviation, no correctness defect

trigger: reviewing WorkflowRoutes::Deps and ScheduleRunner::Deps' sibling closure field names
summary: command_dispatch_concurrency_fn did not match ScheduleRunner::Deps::dispatch_fn_concurrency's established <verb>_fn_<modifier> append-only naming convention.
classification_rationale: naming-convention deviation, no behavioral defect

trigger: an operator wants to observe concurrency claim exclusions, reconciler health, or force-releases
summary: no Prometheus signals existed for claim exclusion, reconciler liveness, anomaly declines, or force-releases -- an operator had no way to see the mechanism working or failing.
classification_rationale: zero observability for a new correctness-relevant mechanism

trigger: reviewing ADR-2002's #2508 background-job replica-safety tracking list
summary: the new concurrency_claims stale-claim reconciler was not added to the #2508 not-yet-HA-compliant background-job list, even though it shares the same class of gap as its siblings.
classification_rationale: new background job untracked against an existing governance list

trigger: reviewing the concurrency_claims migration comment
summary: a migration comment called the whole table EPHEMERAL, overstating transience -- released rows are never deleted, only open rows are short-lived.
classification_rationale: wording overstated the table's actual retention behavior

trigger: an auditor asks why concurrency_claims has no retention/prune policy
summary: no explicit retention-decision statement existed for the new table's unbounded growth (released rows never deleted) -- a defensible choice, but undocumented as a deliberate one.
classification_rationale: retention rationale not recorded despite being a real design decision

trigger: claim_concurrency_slots succeeds but the subsequent send_to() call fails (agent went offline between claim and send)
summary: an orphaned claim with no corresponding in-flight execution, self-heals via the TTL reconciler. Explicitly recommended by chaos-injector as non-blocking, deferred.
classification_rationale: self-healing via existing TTL mechanism, no immediate fix needed

trigger: a second server replica exists and both attempt sync_entra concurrently
summary: the in-process std::atomic<bool> guard only protects one server process -- documented as a known single-server-only limitation, matches the ADR-2002 forward-pointer pattern used throughout the PG-migration ladder.
classification_rationale: documented single-server design limitation, HA is a separate workstream

trigger: a future engineer reads ADR-0066's Mechanism/Release section without awareness of the UP-1 fix
summary: the ADR's own design narrative still said mark_cancelled bulk-releases every open claim -- the exact behavior the Gate 7 fix round deleted to close UP-1. A reader 'restoring consistency' with the stale doc would reintroduce the duplicate-dispatch race UP-1 fixed. Independently found by docs-writer (MUST-FIX #1) and compliance-officer (rated HIGH).
classification_rationale: ADR prose directly contradicted the code shipped in the same fix round

trigger: a healthy server that has never had a concurrency skip/decline/force-release is scraped for /metrics
summary: yuzu_server_dispatch_concurrency_skipped_total, _reconcile_declined_total, and _claim_force_released_total were created lazily inside conditional branches, never describe()'d or pre-seeded at boot, unlike the sibling yuzu_schedule_concurrency_mode_lookup_failed_total added in the same commit. On a healthy fleet the series were structurally absent, not present-at-zero, defeating absent()-based alerting. Independently found by security-guardian, cpp-expert, consistency-auditor, sre, compliance-officer, unhappy-path, and happy-path (7-way convergence -- the strongest confidence signal this pipeline produces).
classification_rationale: new metrics shipped without the codebase's own established pre-seed convention

trigger: an operator reads ADR-0066 or upgrading.md for the stale-claim TTL bound
summary: the wire-expiry clamp added in the Gate 7 fix round (std::clamp to at most 1 hour) was not reflected in the ADR's or upgrading.md's description of stale-claim TTL bounds, both of which still described an unbounded caller-supplied expiry.
classification_rationale: doc not updated for a code change in the same fix round

trigger: an operator reads the new Directory Sync 409 guard description
summary: 'gets an immediate 409 Conflict -- no queueing, no blocking, and it does not itself return until the sync in front of it finishes' -- self-contradictory (an immediate 409 returns immediately; the clause says the opposite).
classification_rationale: a single sentence asserted two mutually exclusive behaviors

trigger: an operator follows the 'see X above' pointer in the new Directory Sync section
summary: two references to 'Diagnosing a stuck KEK op lock above' were backwards -- that section is below the new Directory Sync section, not above.
classification_rationale: directional cross-reference pointed the wrong way

trigger: a future #2508 triager reads the ADR-2002 parenthetical to scope remaining work
summary: the fix-round's own #2508 addition claimed concurrency_claims was missing clock-guard part 2 (persisted anchor) -- actually satisfied via retention_meta. The real gap is the separate SINGLE-WRITER/ADR-0012-advisory-lock requirement. Independently found by consistency-auditor, sre, and compliance-officer.
classification_rationale: self-assessment named the wrong missing requirement, risking mis-scoped remediation

trigger: a per-device dispatch targets a device that is already quarantined at the moment of dispatch
summary: claim_fn runs strictly before dispatch_confined_arms' containment gate -- an already-quarantined device still wins a claim, burning a slot for work that never happens, distinct from the already-documented mid-flight-quarantine case. Independently found by consistency-auditor and happy-path.
classification_rationale: a second instance of the residual-gap class not yet documented

trigger: reviewing the prior round's EPHEMERAL-comment fix for completeness
summary: two residual instances of the same 'ephemeral claim table' overstatement the prior round's fix addressed in one location (execution_tracker.cpp) were left stale in execution_tracker.hpp and ADR-0066's Mechanism heading -- now self-contradicting the same round's own new Retention section. Independently found by sre and compliance-officer.
classification_rationale: a fix applied in one location, sibling copies left stale in the same commit

trigger: a reader compares claim_concurrency_slots' fail-closed pool-exhaustion behavior against ScheduleRunner's fail-open lookup-failure behavior
summary: the ADR gave no rationale for why these two failure modes deliberately diverge (fail-closed vs fail-open) -- both are correct and deliberate, but only one was explained.
classification_rationale: a real design decision left unexplained, inviting a future 'fix' that breaks either

trigger: an operator reads instructions.md/yaml-dsl-spec.md's claim-release description
summary: neither doc stated that cancelling an execution does not release its claim, or that workflow-step-origin per-device claims are release-by-TTL-only even on ordinary success -- both real, user-visible consequences of the shipped design. Independently found by docs-writer and unhappy-path (the cancel half).
classification_rationale: real operational consequences of the shipped design left undocumented

trigger: an operator reads rest-api.md's documentation of the /api/instructions/:id/execute 503 body
summary: the reference doc still said the undifferentiated 503 covered 'all three conditions' after the Gate 7 fix round added a fourth cause (concurrency-claim exclusion) to that same message text.
classification_rationale: reference doc not updated for a message-text change in the same fix round

trigger: an operator looks up the new concurrency metrics in the standard per-feature catalog
summary: none of the 5 new concurrency-related metrics appeared in the per-feature metrics catalog every comparable feature has a dedicated section for. Independently noted by docs-writer and sre.
classification_rationale: new metrics shipped without the codebase's own catalog documentation convention

trigger: a future revert or refactor of the filter-before-claim ordering fix
summary: no test pairs a restrictive VisibleSet with a live claim_fn to prove an out-of-scope agent can never win a claim -- the shipped fix is correct by code read, but revert-fragile. Independently found by security-guardian and unhappy-path.
classification_rationale: the correct fix has no dedicated regression test

trigger: a device is denied by the containment gate after already winning a concurrency claim (either residual-gap variant)
summary: no fast-release hook exists for a claim whose owning agent is denied by containment -- it ages out at TTL instead. A concrete cheaper fix (release outcome.denied_quarantined ids right after wire_and_dispatch_confined returns) is recorded as a Follow-up, not implemented.
classification_rationale: self-healing via existing TTL mechanism, improvement deferred

trigger: reviewing include ordering conventions in test_dispatch_confined_arms.cpp
summary: a new #include was added mid-file rather than the top-of-file block -- but the file already establishes this as local precedent (agent_registry.hpp is included mid-file too, pre-existing), so left as-is to match local convention rather than fixed.
classification_rationale: cosmetic, matches an existing local pattern in the same file
waiver_rationale: matches pre-existing mid-file include precedent in the same file (agent_registry.hpp); fixing only the new one would be inconsistent with the file's own established style
